title: Batch Handoff Stride Lab Notes
content:
Goal:
- Quick personal lab notes exploring an odd p99 spike seen on small-request workloads when stride-based batch handoff is enabled. Trying to capture reproducible steps and quick hypotheses so we can iterate with infra and scheduler folks.

Background / symptom:
- Production alert: intermittent p99 ~1500ms on the small-text gen route (avg ~90ms). QPS steady ~28.
- Alert correlates with a handful of requests being held for an extra batch cycle when a stride handoff occurs between active workers.
- Suspect: stride scheduler moves a request (or KV shard) between internal groups which delays KV cache warming + scheduling alignment, causing an extra 1x batch-time delay.

Experiment environment:
- Local perf cluster (4x A10G equiv), runtime dev image (git: feature/stride-reorg), model: small-ggml-v2-like (seq 512, kv cache enabled), token avg: 32, prompt size small.
- Ingress: custom load generator (node) with deterministic arrival trace (zipf alpha 1.2 + Poisson peak).
- Two scheduler modes toggled: stride-handoff=on / stride-handoff=off.
- Measurement window: 30 minutes each, warmup 5 minutes. Export: per-request latency, batch size, batch id, worker id, kv-hit (bool).

Commands (runnable):
- start cluster: ./scripts/dev-cluster up --nodes 4 --image feature/stride-reorg
- run load: node tools/loadgen.js --trace traces/small-zipf-28qps.json --duration 1800 --out st1.json
- collect: python tools/collect_trace.py --input st1.json --output st1.csv

Key Observations (raw):
- stride-handoff=off: median 72ms, p95 210ms, p99 310ms, throughput stable 27.9 qps
- stride-handoff=on: median 78ms, p95 235ms, p99 1480ms, throughput stable 28.1 qps
- p99 cases when on: batch size often 1 or 2, batch_id transitions (handoff) show request moved between worker-2 -> worker-0 during KV reattach. KV-hit=false on first token after handoff, then true afterwards.

Small table (aggregate):
- mode | median | p95 | p99 | qps
- off  | 72ms   | 210ms| 310ms| 27.9
- on   | 78ms   | 235ms| 1480ms| 28.1

Trace-level notes: (examples)
- trace A: at t=1523.2s request R#3423 assigned to worker-2, queued 7ms, then stride reassign at t+18ms -> worker-0 where it waits for next batch start (+1x batch interval ~= 1s). KV attach completes after first token, causing extra token latency.
- trace B: handoff occurs during concurrent eviction cycle on worker-0 which worsens cold-kv penalty (evictions + re-populate).

Hypotheses:
1) Handoff timing aligns poorly with batch boundary; when a request moves right before a batch flush it misses the current batch and waits for the next, incurring ~1 batch interval delay.
2) KV reattachment cost is non-trivial for small requests (dominates p99).
3) Worker-local priority queueing + handoff race can cause thundering of small single-request batches to fall into slow path.

Quick mitigations tried (dev):
- soft-hold window (200ms): when receiving a handoff, immediately try to steal current in-flight batch on destination worker if still open -> reduces p99 to ~540ms but introduces rare duplicate-token microretries (needs idempotency handling).
- eager-kv-prefetch: ship a tiny KV header at handoff to hint destination to pre-populate -> p99 ~380ms but increases cross-worker bandwidth marginally.
- disable handoff for single-token estimated requests -> p99 ~320ms but loses load distribution gains.

Notes + mental model sketches:
- stride scheduler tries to balance steady-state throughput by moving low-util shards across workers. For microburst small-request nets it improves fairness but when combined with strict batch timing it can misalign requests by a whole interval.
- there are 3 latency contributors for a handed-off request: (A) transfer/comm cost, (B) missed-batch penalty (~batch-interval), (C) cold-kv penalty. A dominates here when seq small and batch-interval ~1s.

Actionable next steps (priority):
- Short-term: add a "handoff grace" check in scheduler: if destination worker has a batch that will start in <200ms, try to enqueue into it instead of waiting for next. (low-risk toggle).
- Mid-term: design a lightweight kv-prefetch contract in the handoff RPC (header-only). Instrument bandwidth and CPU cost tradeoffs.
- Long-term: revisit stride heuristics: prefer handoff when predicted request duration > 250ms OR when batch-interval < 300ms.

Questions for Evan / infra: 
- can we get per-worker batch start-phase telemetry in prod? (would help correlate).
- how costly is an additional 200ms of cross-worker prefetch in terms of network/CPU? (Maya had numbers earlier, ask her to paste).

Misc quick TODOs:
- upload st1.csv to the shared debug bucket and add link to JIRA-INF-3245.
- prepare a narrow PR with "handoff grace" flag behind feature toggle.
- sanity-check idempotency for the steal-into-open-batch flow (duplicate-token guard).

Personal notes:
- This is rough — want to keep this as a readable slice for on-call handover. If we can get telemetry on batch-phase in prod we can reduce speculation.
- I like eager-kv-prefetch as a low-latency friendly approach but need to test the bandwidth cost on large fleets.

End of notes.

Appendix: quick grep of traces (example lines)
- R3423 | assigned worker-2 | queued 7ms | reassign->worker-0 @+18ms | wait 1008ms | first token latency 1012ms | kv-hit false
- R4071 | assigned worker-1 | no reassign | queued 5ms | first token latency 55ms | kv-hit true

-- Kiro
